title: Application Entry Point
content: application entry point  this file serves as the main entry point for the devtinder backend application. it initializes the express server, sets up middleware, configures crossorigin resource sharing (cors), connects to the database, and integrates websocket functionality.   overview  the app.js file is responsible for bootstrapping the entire backend application. it orchestrates the setup of core functionalities including http server creation, database connection, api routing, and realtime communication via websockets. this file ensures that all necessary components are initialized and configured before the server starts listening for incoming requests.   cors configuration  crossorigin resource sharing (cors) is configured to allow requests from specific frontend origins.  <info   this configuration ensures that only trusted frontend applications can interact with the backend api, enhancing security. </info  the following origins are permitted:    http://localhost:5173 (for local development)    https://devtinder.yashwant.xyz (for the deployed production environment)   middleware and routing  the application utilizes several middleware functions and registers various api routes.  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="json body parsing" icon=" {} "     enables the server to parse incoming json request bodies.   </card   <card title="cookie parsing" icon=" 🍪 "     allows the server to parse cookies from incoming requests.   </card </cardgroup  the following routes are mounted to handle specific api endpoints:  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="authentication" icon=" 🔑 "     handles user registration, login, and token management. (src/routes/auth.js)   </card   <card title="profile management" icon=" 👤 "     manages user profile updates and retrieval. (src/routes/profile.js)   </card   <card title="connection requests" icon=" 🤝 "     handles logic for sending and accepting connection requests. (src/routes/requests.js)   </card   <card title="user management" icon=" 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 "     provides endpoints for general userrelated operations. (src/routes/user.js)   </card   <card title="payment processing" icon=" 💰 "     integrates with payment gateways for transactions. (src/routes/payment.js)   </card   <card title="chat functionality" icon=" 💬 "     manages realtime chat features. (src/routes/chat.js)   </card </cardgroup   websocket integration  realtime communication is enabled through websockets. the initializesocket function from src/utils/socket.js is used to set up the websocket server, which is attached to the http server instance.  <tip   websockets are crucial for features like live chat and instant notifications. </tip   database connection and server initialization  the application first establishes a connection to the database using the connectdb function from src/config/database.js. once the database connection is successful, the http server begins listening on port 5000.  <steps   <step title="initialize express app"     creates an express application instance.   </step   <step title="configure cors"     sets up allowed origins for crossorigin requests.   </step   <step title="setup middleware"     initializes express.json() for json body parsing and cookieparser() for cookie parsing.   </step   <step title="register api routes"     mounts all defined routers to their respective base paths.   </step   <step title="create http server"     creates an http server instance using the express app.   </step   <step title="initialize websockets"     integrates the websocket server for realtime features.   </step   <step title="connect to database"     establishes a connection to the mongodb database.   </step   <step title="start server"     begins listening for incoming requests on port 5000.   </step </steps  <warning   if the database connection fails, the server will not start, and an error message will be logged. </warning

title: Database Configuration
content: database configuration  this file contains the necessary configuration and logic to establish a connection to the mongodb database using mongoose.   overview  the database.js module is responsible for initializing and managing the connection to the mongodb instance. it ensures that the application can reliably interact with the database by abstracting the connection logic and utilizing environment variables for sensitive credentials. this module is crucial for all data persistence operations within the application.   database connection  the connectdb function handles the connection to the mongodb database. it uses mongoose to establish a connection using a connection string retrieved from environment variables.  <steps   <step title="retrieve connection string"     the function reads the mongodb connection string from the db_connection_secret environment variable. this variable should contain the full connection uri, including username, password, host, and database name.   </step   <step title="establish mongoose connection"     mongoose's connect method is called with the retrieved connection string to establish a connection to the mongodb server.   </step   <step title="export connection function"     the connectdb function is exported, allowing other parts of the application to call it during the initialization phase.   </step </steps   connectdb()  establishes a connection to the mongodb database.  <warning   the db_connection_secret environment variable must be correctly configured with a valid mongodb connection string. failure to do so will prevent the application from connecting to the database. </warning  javascript javascript const connectdb = async () = {   await mongoose.connect(process.env.db_connection_secret); };  module.exports = connectdb;    usage example  to connect to the database, import the connectdb function and call it during your application's startup process. it's recommended to do this in your main application file (e.g., app.js).  javascript javascript // src/app.js const express = require('express'); const connectdb = require('./config/database');  const app = express();  // connect to the database connectdb().then(() = {   console.log('mongodb connected successfully.'); }).catch((err) = {   console.error('mongodb connection error:', err);   process.exit(1); // exit process with failure });  // ... other application setup and routes

title: Authentication Middleware
content: authentication middleware  this middleware handles user authentication by verifying jwt tokens provided in request cookies, ensuring that only authenticated users can access protected resources.   overview  the auth.js middleware plays a crucial role in securing api endpoints by verifying the authenticity of incoming requests. it extracts a jwt from the request's cookies, validates it against a secret key, and then retrieves the corresponding user from the database. if successful, it attaches the user object to the request for subsequent middleware or route handlers to use.   parameters / configuration  this middleware does not accept direct configuration parameters. it relies on environment variables for its operation.  <warning   the jwt secret is a critical security parameter. ensure process.env.jwt_secret is set securely and is not exposed. </warning <info   this middleware relies on the presence of a jwt token in the request's cookies. for more information on cookie handling, refer to the documentation for your cookie parsing middleware. </info   user authentication middleware (userauth)  verifies a jwt token from request cookies to authenticate a user.  this middleware is used to protect routes that require user authentication. it extracts a jwt from the token cookie, verifies its validity using process.env.jwt_secret, and then attempts to find the associated user in the database using the user model. if successful, the user object is attached to the req.user property, and the request proceeds to the next middleware or route handler. if any step fails (e.g., missing token, invalid token, user not found), an appropriate error response is sent.   parameters  <paramfield name="req" type="object" required   the express request object.   <expandable title="req properties"     <paramfield name="req.cookies" type="object"       an object containing cookies sent with the request. expected to contain a token property.     </paramfield   </expandable </paramfield <paramfield name="res" type="object" required   the express response object. </paramfield <paramfield name="next" type="function" required   the next middleware function in the stack. </paramfield   security and data risks  <warning   exposure of the jwt_secret can lead to the forging of authentication tokens, compromising user accounts and data. </warning <warning   if the token is invalid or expired, sensitive operations will be blocked, but user data remains protected. </warning   usage example  this middleware is typically used in route definitions to protect specific endpoints.  javascript // example usage in src/routes/user.js const express = require('express'); const { userauth } = require('../middleware/auth'); const user = require('../models/user');  const router = express.router();  // protected route: requires authentication router.get('/profile', userauth, async (req, res) = {   // access user details from req.user, which was populated by userauth   res.json({ message: 'welcome to your profile!', user: req.user }); });  module.exports = router;    common errors / troubleshooting  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="error: please login!"     this error occurs when the token cookie is not found in the request. ensure that a jwt token is being set in the cookies after a successful login and that your cookieparsing middleware is correctly configured.   </accordion   <accordion title="error: error: jwt malformed"     this indicates that the jwt token provided is not in the correct format. this could be due to corruption or an incorrect token being sent.   </accordion   <accordion title="error: error: user not found"     this means the user id extracted from the jwt does not correspond to any existing user in the database. this could happen if a user account was deleted after the token was issued.   </accordion   <accordion title="error: invalid signature"     this error signifies that the jwt signature is invalid, meaning the token has been tampered with or was signed with a different secret key.   </accordion </accordiongroup

title: Chat Model
content: chat model  this file defines the mongoose schema and model for managing chat conversations and messages within the application.   overview  the chat model is responsible for storing and retrieving chat data, including participant information and the history of messages exchanged between users. it interacts with the user model through references.  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="participants" icon="👥"     stores objectids referencing the user model for each participant in a chat.   </card   <card title="messages" icon="💬"     contains an array of message objects, each with sender information and text content.   </card </cardgroup   chat schema  the chatschema defines the structure of a chat document in the mongodb collection.   participants  <paramfield name="participants" type="array<objectid" required   an array of objectids, each referencing a user document. these represent the users involved in the chat conversation. </paramfield   messages  <paramfield name="messages" type="array<object" required   an array of message objects, where each object conforms to the messageschema.   <expandable title="messageschema properties"     <paramfield name="senderid" type="objectid" required       the id of the user who sent the message. this is a reference to the user model.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="text" type="string" required       the content of the message.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="createdat" type="date"       timestamp indicating when the message was created. automatically managed by mongoose.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="updatedat" type="date"       timestamp indicating when the message was last updated. automatically managed by mongoose.     </paramfield   </expandable </paramfield   model export  the chat model is exported for use in other parts of the application.  javascript const mongoose = require("mongoose");  const messageschema = new mongoose.schema(     {         senderid: {             type: mongoose.schema.types.objectid,             ref: "user",             required: true,         },          text: {             type: string,             required: true,         },     },     { timestamps: true } )  const chatschema = new mongoose.schema(     {         participants: [             { type: mongoose.schema.types.objectid, ref: "user", required: true },         ],         messages: [messageschema]     } )  const chat = mongoose.model("chat", chatschema);  module.exports =  { chat }    usage  this model is typically imported and used within src/routes/chat.js to manage chatrelated operations, such as creating new chats, adding messages, and retrieving chat history.  javascript // example usage in src/routes/chat.js (conceptual) const { chat } = require('../models/chat'); const { user } = require('../models/user'); // assuming user model is available  // ... (other route handlers)  // to create a new chat async function createchat(userid1, userid2) {   const newchat = new chat({     participants: [userid1, userid2],     messages: []   });   await newchat.save();   return newchat; }  // to add a message to an existing chat async function addmessagetochat(chatid, senderid, messagetext) {   const updatedchat = await chat.findbyidandupdate(     chatid,     {       $push: {         messages: { senderid: senderid, text: messagetext }       }     },     { new: true }   );   return updatedchat; }

title: Connection Request Model
content: connection request model  this file defines the mongoose schema and model for managing connection requests between users. it handles the storage and validation of incoming requests, including their status and sender/receiver information.   overview  the connectionrequestmodel is a critical component for managing user interactions within the application. it models the relationship where one user expresses interest, accepts, rejects, or ignores a request from another user. this model is used by the requests routes to process and update the status of these interactions.  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="user references" icon="👤"     establishes relationships with the <codeuser</code model to link requests to specific users.   </card   <card title="status management" icon="✅"     enforces predefined statuses for connection requests, ensuring data integrity.   </card </cardgroup   parameters / configuration  this model does not accept direct configuration parameters. it is used internally by the application's data layer.   connectionrequest model  this is the mongoose model for connectionrequest documents.  <responsefield name="fromuserid" type="objectid" required   the id of the user sending the connection request. this references the <codeuser</code model. </responsefield  <responsefield name="touserid" type="objectid" required   the id of the user receiving the connection request. this references the <codeuser</code model. </responsefield  <responsefield name="status" type="string" required   the current status of the connection request. must be one of: "ignored", "interested", "accepted", "rejected". </responsefield  <responsefield name="createdat" type="date"   timestamp indicating when the connection request was created. automatically managed by mongoose. </responsefield  <responsefield name="updatedat" type="date"   timestamp indicating when the connection request was last updated. automatically managed by mongoose. </responsefield  <warning   the fromuserid and touserid fields must not be the same. the model prevents sending a connection request to oneself. </warning   usage example  while this is a model, it's typically used within service layers or routes. here's an example of how you might create a new connection request:  javascript const connectionrequest = require('../models/connectionrequest'); const mongoose = require('mongoose');  async function createconnectionrequest(fromuserid, touserid) {   try {     const newrequest = new connectionrequest({       fromuserid: new mongoose.types.objectid(fromuserid),       touserid: new mongoose.types.objectid(touserid),       status: "interested", // initial status     });      const savedrequest = await newrequest.save();     console.log("connection request created:", savedrequest);     return savedrequest;   } catch (error) {     console.error("error creating connection request:", error.message);     throw error;   } }  // example usage (assuming you have valid user ids) // createconnectionrequest("user123", "user456");    common errors / troubleshooting  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="error: cannot send connection request to yourself!"     this error occurs when the fromuserid and touserid are identical. the schema's presave hook prevents this to avoid illogical requests. ensure that the ids passed to the model constructor are distinct.   </accordion   <accordion title="error: [value] is incorrect status type"     this error means that the status field was assigned a value not present in the enum array (ignored, interested, accepted, rejected). ensure you are using one of the allowed string values for the status.   </accordion </accordiongroup

title: Payment Model
content: payment model  this file defines the mongoose schema and model for storing payment transaction details. it outlines the structure of payment records within the application's database.   overview  the payment model is responsible for persisting all information related to financial transactions, including user associations, payment provider identifiers, order details, and financial specifics like amount and currency. it is used across the application to track successful payments, typically initiated through the payment.js route.   parameters / configuration  this model does not accept direct configuration parameters. it defines the database schema for payment records.   fields  the payment model uses the following schema fields:   userid  <paramfield name="userid" type="objectid" ref="user" required   the unique identifier of the user associated with this payment. this field links to the user model. </paramfield   paymentid  <paramfield name="paymentid" type="string"   the unique identifier provided by the payment gateway (e.g., razorpay payment id). </paramfield   orderid  <paramfield name="orderid" type="string" required   the unique identifier for the order generated by the payment gateway. </paramfield   status  <paramfield name="status" type="string" required   the current status of the payment transaction (e.g., "paid", "failed", "pending"). </paramfield   amount  <paramfield name="amount" type="number" required   the total amount of the transaction in the smallest currency unit (e.g., paise for inr). </paramfield   currency  <paramfield name="currency" type="string" required   the currency in which the payment was made (e.g., "inr", "usd"). </paramfield   receipt  <paramfield name="receipt" type="string" required   a unique identifier for the transaction receipt generated by the payment gateway. </paramfield   notes  <paramfield name="notes" type="object"   an object containing additional information related to the payment.   <expandable title="notes properties"     <paramfield name="notes.firstname" type="string"the first name of the user at the time of payment.</paramfield     <paramfield name="notes.lastname" type="string"the last name of the user at the time of payment.</paramfield     <paramfield name="notes.membershiptype" type="string"the type of membership purchased during this transaction.</paramfield   </expandable </paramfield  the schema also includes timestamps: true, which automatically adds createdat and updatedat fields to each document.   usage example  this model is typically used within the payment.js route handler to save transaction details after a successful payment confirmation.  javascript // example usage in src/routes/payment.js (conceptual) const payment = require('../models/payment'); const mongoose = require('mongoose');  async function handlesuccessfulpayment(paymentdetails, user) {   const newpayment = new payment({     userid: user._id,     paymentid: paymentdetails.razorpay_payment_id,     orderid: paymentdetails.razorpay_order_id,     status: 'paid',     amount: paymentdetails.amount,     currency: 'inr', // assuming inr for this example     receipt: paymentdetails.razorpay_receipt,     notes: {       firstname: user.firstname,       lastname: user.lastname,       membershiptype: 'premium', // example membership type     },   });    try {     await newpayment.save();     console.log('payment record saved successfully:', newpayment._id);     // further actions like upgrading user subscription   } catch (error) {     console.error('error saving payment record:', error);     // handle error appropriately   } }    common errors / troubleshooting  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="what happens if a payment record fails to save?"     if an error occurs during the newpayment.save() operation, the catch block in the example usage will be triggered. this indicates a database issue, such as connectivity problems or schema validation errors. the error should be logged, and appropriate fallback mechanisms should be implemented, such as notifying an administrator or retrying the operation if feasible.   </accordion   <accordion title="how are payment statuses updated?"     the status field should be updated based on the responses received from the payment gateway. for instance, if the payment gateway confirms a successful transaction, the status would be set to "paid". if a transaction fails at any point, the status should be updated accordingly (e.g., "failed"). this logic typically resides within the route handler that processes the payment gateway's callbacks or webhooks.   </accordion </accordiongroup

title: User Model
content: user model  this file defines the mongoose schema and methods for user data, handling user authentication, profile information, and related logic.   overview  the user model is central to the application, representing individual users. it includes fields for profile details, authentication credentials, and user status (e.g., premium membership). this model interacts with the database to store and retrieve user information and provides methods for generating jwts and validating passwords.  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="schema definition" icon="📝"     defines the structure and validation rules for user data stored in mongodb.   </card   <card title="authentication methods" icon="🔑"     includes methods for generating json web tokens (jwts) and verifying user passwords using bcrypt.   </card </cardgroup   user schema fields  this section details the fields within the user schema, their types, validation rules, and default values.  <cardgroup cols={3}   <card title="basic information" icon="👤"     <paramfield name="firstname" type="string" required minlength={4} maxlength={50}       the user's first name.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="lastname" type="string"       the user's last name.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="emailid" type="string" required unique lowercase trim       the user's email address. must be a valid email format and will be unique across all users.     </paramfield   </card   <card title="authentication" icon="🔒"     <paramfield name="password" type="string" required       the user's password. must meet strong password criteria (e.g., minimum length, mix of characters).     </paramfield   </card   <card title="profile details" icon="ℹ️"     <paramfield name="age" type="number" min={18}       the user's age. must be 18 or older.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="gender" type="string"       the user's gender. accepted values: "male", "female", "other".     </paramfield     <paramfield name="photourl" type="string" default="https://m.mediaamazon.com/images/m/mv5bmmrlnmi5ywetmja5oc00ngm4lwjjmgutzju0nmi2mzrlognhxkeyxkfqcgc@._v1_.jpg"       a url pointing to the user's profile picture. must be a valid url.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="about" type="string" default="this is a default abouth of the user!"       a short biography or description of the user.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="skills" type="[string]"       an array of strings representing the user's skills.     </paramfield   </card   <card title="membership" icon="🌟"     <paramfield name="ispremium" type="boolean" default={false}       indicates if the user has a premium membership.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="membershiptype" type="string"       the type of membership the user has (e.g., "monthly", "yearly").     </paramfield   </card </cardgroup   methods   getjwt  generates a json web token (jwt) for the user.  javascript userschema.methods.getjwt = async function () {     const user = this;      const token = await jwt.sign({ _id: user._id }, "dev@tinder$790", {                 expiresin: "1d"             });              return token; }   <note the jwt secret dev@tinder$790 should be stored securely in environment variables and not hardcoded. </note   validatepassword  compares a provided password against the user's hashed password.  javascript userschema.methods.validatepassword = async function (passwordinputbyuser) {     const user = this;     const passwordhash = user.password;      const ispasswordvaild = await bcrypt.compare(passwordinputbyuser, passwordhash);      return ispasswordvaild; }   <warning ensure that passwords are always hashed using bcrypt before storing them in the database. </warning   usage example  this model is typically used in authentication routes (e.g., src/routes/auth.js) and controllers to find, create, or update user records.  here's an example of how you might use the user model to find a user and generate a token:  javascript const user = require('../models/user');  async function loginuser(email, password) {   try {     const user = await user.findone({ emailid: email });      if (!user) {       throw new error('invalid login credentials');     }      const ismatch = await user.validatepassword(password);      if (!ismatch) {       throw new error('invalid login credentials');     }      const token = await user.getjwt();     return { user, token };    } catch (error) {     console.error("login error:", error);     throw error; // rethrow the error to be handled by the caller   } }   <tip it's recommended to use environment variables for sensitive information like jwt secrets to enhance security. </tip   indexing  the schema includes an index on firstname and lastname to optimize queries that involve both fields.  javascript userschema.index({ firstname: 1, lastname: 1 })    exports  this model is exported for use in other parts of the application.  javascript module.exports = mongoose.model("user", userschema);

title: Authentication Routes
content: authentication routes  this file defines the api endpoints for user authentication, including signup, login, and logout functionality. it integrates with the user model for data storage and uses bcrypt for password encryption.   overview  the authentication module provides the core api endpoints for managing user accounts. it handles user registration, secure login with token generation, and session termination via logout. this module relies on the user model for database interactions and utilizes utility functions for data validation and password hashing.   signup  handles new user registration.   post /signup  creates a new user account.  <paramfield name="firstname" type="string" required   the user's first name. </paramfield <paramfield name="lastname" type="string" required   the user's last name. </paramfield <paramfield name="emailid" type="string" required   the user's unique email address. </paramfield <paramfield name="password" type="string" required   the user's desired password. minimum 8 characters recommended. </paramfield <paramfield name="age" type="number" required   the user's age. </paramfield <paramfield name="gender" type="string" required   the user's gender. </paramfield <paramfield name="about" type="string" default="tell us about yourself"   a short bio or description from the user. </paramfield <paramfield name="skills" type="array" default=[]   an array of the user's skills. </paramfield <paramfield name="photourl" type="string"   a url pointing to the user's profile picture. </paramfield  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "message": "user added sucessfully!",   "data": {     "_id": "60d5ec49f2c1b3001f8e3e3e",     "firstname": "john",     "lastname": "doe",     "emailid": "john.doe@example.com",     "age": 30,     "gender": "male",     "about": "software engineer with a passion for building scalable applications.",     "skills": ["javascript", "node.js", "react"],     "photourl": "https://example.com/photos/john_doe.jpg",     "__v": 0   } }  </responseexample  <warning   sensitive user data is handled. ensure proper security measures are in place for data transmission and storage. the password is automatically hashed using bcrypt. </warning   usage example  javascript // example using fetch api fetch('/api/auth/signup', {   method: 'post',   headers: {     'contenttype': 'application/json',   },   body: json.stringify({     firstname: 'jane',     lastname: 'smith',     emailid: 'jane.smith@example.com',     password: 'securepassword123!',     age: 28,     gender: 'female',     about: 'enthusiastic designer and artist.',     skills: ['ui/ux', 'figma', 'illustration'],     photourl: 'https://example.com/photos/jane_smith.jpg',   }), }) .then(response = response.json()) .then(data = console.log(data)) .catch(error = console.error('error:', error));    login  handles user authentication.   post /login  authenticates a user and returns a session token.  <paramfield name="emailid" type="string" required   the user's registered email address. </paramfield <paramfield name="password" type="string" required   the user's password. </paramfield  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "_id": "60d5ec49f2c1b3001f8e3e3e",   "firstname": "john",   "lastname": "doe",   "emailid": "john.doe@example.com",   "age": 30,   "gender": "male",   "about": "software engineer with a passion for building scalable applications.",   "skills": ["javascript", "node.js", "react"],   "photourl": "https://example.com/photos/john_doe.jpg",   "__v": 0 }  </responseexample  <warning   invalid credentials will result in an error. ensure the emailid and password are correct. the response includes the authenticated user object. </warning   usage example  javascript // example using fetch api fetch('/api/auth/login', {   method: 'post',   headers: {     'contenttype': 'application/json',   },   body: json.stringify({     emailid: 'john.doe@example.com',     password: 'securepassword123!',   }), }) .then(response = response.json()) .then(data = console.log('login successful:', data)) .catch(error = console.error('login error:', error));    logout  handles user session termination.   post /logout  clears the authentication token, effectively logging the user out.  <responseexample text 200 ok logout sucessful!!  </responseexample  <tip   this endpoint clears the token cookie. for robust session management in production, consider implementing token blacklisting or shortlived tokens with refresh mechanisms. </tip   usage example  javascript // example using fetch api fetch('/api/auth/logout', {   method: 'post', }) .then(response = response.text()) .then(message = console.log(message)) .catch(error = console.error('logout error:', error));

title: Chat Routes
content: chat routes  handles all chatrelated operations, including fetching existing conversations, creating new ones, and retrieving messages. this module interacts with the chat model and leverages user authentication middleware.   overview  the chat.js file defines api endpoints for managing usertouser conversations. it allows users to retrieve chat history with another user and facilitates the creation of new chat threads when none exist.  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="get chat history" icon="💬"     retrieves an existing chat conversation or creates a new one.   </card </cardgroup   routes   get chat history or create new  this endpoint retrieves an existing chat conversation between the authenticated user and a specified targetuserid. if no chat exists, it creates a new one.   parameters  <paramfield name="targetuserid" type="string" required   the id of the user with whom to chat. </paramfield   request example  <requestexample bash curl curl x get https://api.example.com/chat/:targetuserid \   h "authorization: bearer <your_jwt_token"  </requestexample   response example  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "_id": "60f3b9b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3",   "participants": ["60f3b9b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b1", "60f3b9b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b2"],   "messages": [     {       "senderid": {         "_id": "60f3b9b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b1",         "firstname": "john",         "lastname": "doe"       },       "content": "hey there!",       "timestamp": "20231027t10:00:00.000z"     }   ],   "createdat": "20231027t10:00:00.000z",   "updatedat": "20231027t10:05:00.000z" }  </responseexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "_id": "60f3b9b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b4",   "participants": ["60f3b9b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b1", "60f3b9b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b2"],   "messages": [],   "createdat": "20231027t10:10:00.000z",   "updatedat": "20231027t10:10:00.000z" }  </responseexample  <info this route requires a valid jwt token in the authorization header for user authentication. </info   usage example  javascript // example usage in another part of the application (e.g., a frontend client)  async function fetchchathistory(targetuserid, token) {   try {     const response = await fetch(/chat/${targetuserid}, {       headers: {         'authorization': bearer ${token}       }     });      if (!response.ok) {       throw new error(http error! status: ${response.status});     }      const chatdata = await response.json();     console.log("chat history:", chatdata);     return chatdata;   } catch (error) {     console.error("failed to fetch chat history:", error);     return null;   } }  // example call: // const usertoken = "your_actual_jwt_token"; // const otheruserid = "some_user_id"; // fetchchathistory(otheruserid, usertoken);    related files  this route interacts with:   src/middleware/auth.js: for user authentication.  src/models/chat.js: for interacting with the chat database collection.

title: Payment Routes
content: payment routes  this file defines the api endpoints for handling payment processing, including creating payment orders and verifying webhook events from razorpay.   overview  this module is responsible for integrating with the razorpay payment gateway to facilitate premium membership purchases. it handles the creation of payment orders, the processing of payment callbacks via webhooks, and the verification of user premium status. it interacts with the payment and user models to update records accordingly.  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="create payment order" icon="🛒"     initiates a new payment order with razorpay for premium membership.   </card   <card title="process webhook" icon="🔁"     handles asynchronous notifications from razorpay regarding payment status updates.   </card   <card title="verify premium status" icon="✅"     checks if a user has an active premium membership.   </card </cardgroup   create payment order  handles the creation of a payment order for a selected membership type.   post /payment/create  this endpoint creates a new payment order using the razorpay api. it requires user authentication.   parameters  <paramfield name="membershiptype" type="string" required   the type of membership to purchase. accepted values are defined in membershipamount (e.g., "monthly", "yearly"). </paramfield   request body  the request body should contain the membershiptype.   response  returns the created razorpay order details and the razorpay api key id.  <requestexample bash curl curl x post https://yourapi.com/payment/create \   h "authorization: bearer <your_jwt_token" \   h "contenttype: application/json" \   d '{"membershiptype": "monthly"}'  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "userid": "user123",   "orderid": "order_abc123",   "status": "created",   "amount": 10000,   "currency": "inr",   "receipt": "receipt1",   "notes": {     "firstname": "john",     "lastname": "doe",     "emailid": "john.doe@example.com",     "membershiptype": "monthly"   },   "keyid": "rzp_test_your_key_id" }   json 400 bad request {   "error": "invalid membership type" }  </responseexample  <tip the amount in the response is in paise. multiply by 100 to get the actual currency value. </tip  <warning ensure the razorpay_key_id environment variable is correctly set in your application's configuration. </warning   process webhook  handles asynchronous notifications from razorpay regarding payment status.   post /payment/webhook  this endpoint is called by razorpay to notify your application about payment events, such as payment.captured or payment.failed.   request body  the request body contains details about the payment event.   security  <warning it is critical to validate the incoming webhook signature to ensure the request originates from razorpay and has not been tampered with. failure to do so can lead to security vulnerabilities. </warning  to validate the signature, use the xrazorpaysignature header and your razorpay_webhook_secret.   response  returns a success message if the webhook is processed correctly.  <requestexample bash curl curl x post https://yourapi.com/payment/webhook \   h "xrazorpaysignature: your_generated_signature" \   h "contenttype: application/json" \   d '{     "payload": {       "payment": {         "entity": {           "id": "pay_abc123",           "order_id": "order_abc123",           "status": "captured",           "amount": 10000,           "currency": "inr",           "notes": {             "firstname": "john",             "lastname": "doe",             "emailid": "john.doe@example.com",             "membershiptype": "monthly"           }         }       }     },     "event": "payment.captured"   }'  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "msg": "webhook received successfully" }   json 400 bad request {   "msg": "invalid webhook signature" }  </responseexample  <info this endpoint uses the razorpayutils library for signature validation. ensure it's installed and configured correctly. </info  <tip you can uncomment the if (req.body.event === "payment.captured ") and if(req.body.event ==="payment.faild") blocks to implement specific logic for different payment events. </tip   verify premium status  checks if a user has an active premium membership.   get /premium/verify  this endpoint verifies the premium status of the currently authenticated user.   authentication  requires user authentication via userauth middleware.   response  returns the user object, including their ispremium status.  <requestexample bash curl curl x get https://yourapi.com/premium/verify \   h "authorization: bearer <your_jwt_token"  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "ispremium": true,   "membershiptype": "monthly",   // ... other user properties }   json 200 ok {   "ispremium": false,   // ... other user properties }  </responseexample  <note this endpoint returns the user object regardless of premium status, but the ispremium flag will indicate their current membership level. </note

title: Profile Management
content: profile management  this file defines routes for managing user profiles, including viewing, editing, and updating passwords. it leverages middleware for authentication and validation utilities for input sanitization.   overview  the profile.js route handler provides endpoints for users to manage their personal information. this includes retrieving their profile details, making updates to their information, and securely changing their password. it integrates with the userauth middleware to ensure only authenticated users can access these functionalities and uses validation helpers to maintain data integrity.   routes   view profile  retrieves the authenticated user's profile information.  method: get path: /profile/view authentication: required (userauth middleware)  this route decodes the jwt from cookies to identify the loggedin user, fetches their details from the database, and returns the user object.  <requestexample bash curl curl x get https://api.example.com/profile/view \   h "cookie: token=your_jwt_token_here"  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "_id": "60f7b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3",   "firstname": "john",   "lastname": "doe",   "email": "john.doe@example.com",   "dob": "19900515t00:00:00.000z",   "gender": "male",   "location": "new york",   "bio": "passionate developer and avid traveler.",   "profilepic": "https://example.com/profile/john.doe.jpg",   "createdat": "20210719t10:00:00.000z",   "updatedat": "20210719t10:00:00.000z",   "__v": 0 }  </responseexample  <responseexample json 400 bad request {   "error": "error: invaild token" }  </responseexample   edit profile  updates the authenticated user's profile information.  method: patch path: /profile/edit authentication: required (userauth middleware)  this route accepts a partial update of the user's profile data from the request body. it validates the input using validateeditprofiledata and then applies the changes to the user object before saving it to the database.  <requestexample bash curl curl x patch https://api.example.com/profile/edit \   h "cookie: token=your_jwt_token_here" \   h "contenttype: application/json" \   d '{     "firstname": "jonathan",     "location": "los angeles",     "bio": "exploring new opportunities."   }'  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "message": "jonathan, your profile is updated sucessfully",   "data": {     "_id": "60f7b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3b3",     "firstname": "jonathan",     "lastname": "doe",     "email": "john.doe@example.com",     "dob": "19900515t00:00:00.000z",     "gender": "male",     "location": "los angeles",     "bio": "exploring new opportunities.",     "profilepic": "https://example.com/profile/john.doe.jpg",     "createdat": "20210719t10:00:00.000z",     "updatedat": "20231027t14:30:00.000z",     "__v": 1   } }  </responseexample  <responseexample json 400 bad request {   "error": "error: invaild edit request" }  </responseexample   update password  changes the authenticated user's password.  method: patch path: /profile/password authentication: required (userauth middleware)  this route allows users to update their password by providing their current password and the new desired password. it validates the new password's strength using validator.isstrongpassword and then securely hashes and updates the password in the database.  <warning   ensure the currentpassword provided matches the user's existing password before attempting to update. incorrect credentials will result in an error. </warning  <requestexample bash curl curl x patch https://api.example.com/profile/password \   h "cookie: token=your_jwt_token_here" \   h "contenttype: application/json" \   d '{     "currentpassword": "oldsecurepassword123",     "newpassword": "newsuperstrongpassword!@"   }'  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok "password changed sucessfully!"  </responseexample  <responseexample json 400 bad request "input fields are required."  </responseexample  <responseexample json 400 bad request "please enter a strong password."  </responseexample   usage example  this example demonstrates how to fetch a user's profile using the /profile/view endpoint.  javascript async function getuserprofile(token) {   try {     const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/profile/view', {       method: 'get',       headers: {         'cookie': token=${token},         'contenttype': 'application/json',       },     });      if (!response.ok) {       const errordata = await response.json();       throw new error(errordata.error || http error! status: ${response.status});     }      const userdata = await response.json();     console.log('user profile:', userdata);     return userdata;   } catch (error) {     console.error('error fetching user profile:', error);     return null;   } }  // example usage: // const usertoken = 'your_jwt_token_here'; // getuserprofile(usertoken);

title: Connection Requests API
content: connection requests api  this file defines the api endpoints for managing connection requests within the application. it handles sending new requests, reviewing pending requests, and ensures all operations are authenticated.   overview  the requests.js file is part of the routes directory and exposes endpoints related to user connection requests. it leverages middleware for authentication and interacts with the connectionrequestmodel and user models to manage request data and user information. this module is crucial for facilitating usertouser interactions and relationship building within the platform.   sending a connection request  this endpoint allows a user to send a connection request to another user with a specified status.   post /request/send/:status/:touserid  initiates a connection request from the authenticated user to another user.  <paramfield name="status" type="string" required   the initial status of the connection request. allowed values are:   <inlinelist type="bullet"     <liignored</li     <liinterested</li   </inlinelist </paramfield  <paramfield name="touserid" type="string" required   the unique identifier of the user to whom the request is being sent. </paramfield  <paramfield name="userauth" type="middleware"   this middleware ensures that the request is authenticated and the req.user object is available. </paramfield  <requestexample bash curl curl x post https://api.example.com/request/send/interested/60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9d \   h "authorization: bearer your_auth_token"  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "message": "john is interested in jane",   "data": {     "_id": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9e",     "fromuserid": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9c",     "touserid": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9d",     "status": "interested",     "createdat": "20231027t10:00:00.000z",     "updatedat": "20231027t10:00:00.000z"   } }  json 400 bad request {   "message": "invalid status type: unknown" }  json 400 bad request {   "message": "connection request already exists" }  json 404 not found {   "message": "user not found!" }  </responseexample  <note   the sendemail utility is commented out in the source code. if uncommented, it would attempt to send an email notification upon successful request creation. </note   reviewing a connection request  this endpoint allows a user to review a pending connection request sent to them.   post /request/review/:status/:requestid  updates the status of a received connection request.  <paramfield name="status" type="string" required   the review status for the connection request. allowed values are:   <inlinelist type="bullet"     <liaccepted</li     <lirejected</li   </inlinelist </paramfield  <paramfield name="requestid" type="string" required   the unique identifier of the connection request to review. </paramfield  <paramfield name="userauth" type="middleware"   this middleware ensures that the request is authenticated and the req.user object is available. the authenticated user must be the touserid of the request. </paramfield  <requestexample bash curl curl x post https://api.example.com/request/review/accepted/60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9e \   h "authorization: bearer your_auth_token"  </requestexample  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "message": "connection request accepted successfully.",   "data": {     "_id": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9e",     "fromuserid": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9c",     "touserid": "60c72b2f9b1e8a001f8e4c9d",     "status": "accepted",     "createdat": "20231027t10:00:00.000z",     "updatedat": "20231027t10:05:00.000z"   } }  json 400 bad request {   "message": "status not allowed!" }  json 404 not found {   "message": "connection request not found" }  </responseexample  <warning   this endpoint only allows reviewing requests that are currently in the "interested" state and are directed to the authenticated user. </warning   usage example  this section demonstrates how to use the connection request routes from a client application.  javascript // example using fetch api in a javascript client  async function sendconnectionrequest(touserid, status = "interested") {   try {     const token = localstorage.getitem("authtoken"); // assuming token is stored locally     const response = await fetch(/request/send/${status}/${touserid}, {       method: "post",       headers: {         "contenttype": "application/json",         "authorization": bearer ${token},       },     });      if (!response.ok) {       const errordata = await response.json();       throw new error(errordata.message || http error! status: ${response.status});     }      const data = await response.json();     console.log("request sent successfully:", data);     return data;   } catch (error) {     console.error("error sending request:", error);   } }  async function reviewconnectionrequest(requestid, status = "accepted") {   try {     const token = localstorage.getitem("authtoken"); // assuming token is stored locally     const response = await fetch(/request/review/${status}/${requestid}, {       method: "post",       headers: {         "contenttype": "application/json",         "authorization": bearer ${token},       },     });      if (!response.ok) {       const errordata = await response.json();       throw new error(errordata.message || http error! status: ${response.status});     }      const data = await response.json();     console.log("request reviewed successfully:", data);     return data;   } catch (error) {     console.error("error reviewing request:", error);   } }  // example usage: // sendconnectionrequest("user_id_to_send_to"); // reviewconnectionrequest("request_id_to_review", "accepted");     common errors  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="400 bad request  invalid status type"     this error occurs when the status parameter in the /request/send endpoint is not one of the allowed values (ignored, interested). ensure you are passing a valid status.   </accordion   <accordion title="400 bad request  connection request already exists"     this error is returned when a connection request between the fromuserid and touserid already exists. you cannot send duplicate requests.   </accordion   <accordion title="404 not found  user not found"     this error indicates that the touserid provided in the /request/send endpoint does not correspond to an existing user in the database.   </accordion   <accordion title="404 not found  connection request not found"     this error occurs in the /request/review endpoint if the requestid does not match any existing connection request, or if the request is not directed to the authenticated user, or if the request is not in the "interested" state.   </accordion </accordiongroup

title: User Routes
content: user routes  this file defines the api routes for userrelated operations, including fetching user data, managing connection requests, and retrieving potential matches for users.   overview  the user.js file acts as the entry point for all userspecific api endpoints within the application. it handles requests related to user profiles, connection requests, and the user feed. it leverages middleware for authentication and interacts with the user and connectionrequestmodel to perform data operations.  <cardgroup cols={2}   <card title="user data retrieval" icon="👤"     endpoints for fetching individual user profiles and listing users for the feed.   </card   <card title="connection management" icon="🤝"     routes for viewing received connection requests and listing accepted connections.   </card </cardgroup   routes   get user by id  retrieves a user's profile information based on their id.   get /user/getuserbyid/:userid  <paramfield name="userid" type="string" required   the unique identifier for the user to retrieve. </paramfield  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "data": {     "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a1",     "firstname": "jane",     "lastname": "doe",     "photourl": "http://example.com/photo.jpg",     "age": 28,     "gender": "female",     "about": "loves hiking and exploring new places.",     "skills": ["hiking", "photography"],     "email": "jane.doe@example.com"   } }   json 404 not found {   "message": "user not found" }   json 500 internal server error {   "message": "server error" }  </responseexample   get received connection requests  fetches all connection requests where the loggedin user is the recipient and the status is "interested".   get /user/requests/received  <infothis route requires authentication via the userauth middleware.</info  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "message": "data fetched successfully",   "data": [     {       "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a2",       "status": "interested",       "fromuserid": {         "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a3",         "firstname": "john",         "lastname": "smith",         "photourl": "http://example.com/john.jpg",         "age": 30,         "gender": "male",         "about": "software engineer and avid gamer.",         "skills": ["javascript", "react", "node.js"]       }     }   ] }  </responseexample   get user connections  retrieves all accepted connection requests involving the loggedin user, either as the sender or recipient.   get /user/connections  <infothis route requires authentication via the userauth middleware.</info  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "data": [     {       "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a4",       "status": "accepted",       "fromuserid": {         "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a3",         "firstname": "john",         "lastname": "smith",         "photourl": "http://example.com/john.jpg",         "age": 30,         "gender": "male",         "about": "software engineer and avid gamer.",         "skills": ["javascript", "react", "node.js"]       },       "touserid": {         "_id": "60d5ec49d3e8a10015f7e2a1",         "firstname": "jane",         "lastname": "doe",         "photourl": "http://example.com/photo.jpg",         "age": 28,         "gender": "female",         "about": "loves hiking and exploring new places.",         "skills": ["hiking", "photography"]       }     }   ] }  </responseexample   get user feed  fetches a paginated list of users that the loggedin user has not yet connected with or sent a request to.   get /user/feed  <infothis route requires authentication via the userauth middleware.</info  <paramfield name="page" type="integer" default="1"   the page number for pagination. </paramfield <paramfield name="limit" type="integer" default="10"   the maximum number of users to return per page. maximum limit is 50. </paramfield  <responseexample json 200 ok {   "data": [     {       "firstname": "peter",       "lastname": "jones",       "photourl": "http://example.com/peter.jpg",       "age": 25,       "gender": "male",       "about": "musician and aspiring chef.",       "skills": ["guitar", "cooking"]     },     {       "firstname": "sarah",       "lastname": "lee",       "photourl": "http://example.com/sarah.jpg",       "age": 29,       "gender": "female",       "about": "travel blogger and photographer.",       "skills": ["travel", "photography", "writing"]     }   ] }  </responseexample   usage example  here's how you might use these user routes in a client application:  <codegroup javascript javascript // example using fetch to get user connections async function getuserconnections(token) {   try {     const response = await fetch("https://yourapi.com/user/connections", {       headers: {         authorization: bearer ${token},       },     });     const data = await response.json();     console.log("user connections:", data.data);     return data.data;   } catch (error) {     console.error("error fetching connections:", error);     throw error;   } }  // example using fetch to get user feed async function getuserfeed(token, page = 1, limit = 10) {   try {     const response = await fetch(https://yourapi.com/user/feed?page=${page}&limit=${limit}, {       headers: {         authorization: bearer ${token},       },     });     const data = await response.json();     console.log("user feed:", data.data);     return data.data;   } catch (error) {     console.error("error fetching user feed:", error);     throw error;   } }   javascript node.js // example using a hypothetical api client for node.js const apiclient = require('./apiclient'); // assuming you have an api client  async function getuserconnections() {   try {     const response = await apiclient.get('/user/connections');     console.log('user connections:', response.data.data);     return response.data.data;   } catch (error) {     console.error('error fetching connections:', error);     throw error;   } }  async function getuserfeed(page = 1, limit = 10) {   try {     const response = await apiclient.get('/user/feed', { params: { page, limit } });     console.log('user feed:', response.data.data);     return response.data.data;   } catch (error) {     console.error('error fetching user feed:', error);     throw error;   } }  </codegroup   common errors / troubleshooting  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="user not found when using /getuserbyid/:userid"     this error typically occurs when the userid provided in the url does not correspond to an existing user in the database. doublecheck that the userid is correct and that the user exists.   </accordion   <accordion title="server error when fetching connections or feed"     a "server error" (500) indicates an unexpected issue on the serverside. this could be due to database connection problems, unhandled exceptions in the route logic, or issues with external service integrations. check server logs for more detailed error messages.   </accordion </accordiongroup

title: Constants
content: constants  this file exports constants used throughout the application, primarily for pricing and configuration values.   overview  this utility file centralizes various constants. currently, it exports pricing information for different membership tiers, which can be leveraged by modules like payment.js and user.js to determine subscription costs.  <cardgroup cols={1}   <card title="membership pricing" icon="💰"     defines monetary values for different membership levels, ensuring consistency across the application.   </card </cardgroup   membership pricing constants  the membershipamount object provides the cost for each membership tier.  <paramfield name="membershipamount" type="object"   an object containing the costs for each membership tier.   <expandable title="membershipamount properties"     <paramfield name="membershipamount.silver" type="number"       the cost of the silver membership tier.     </paramfield     <paramfield name="membershipamount.gold" type="number"       the cost of the gold membership tier.     </paramfield   </expandable </paramfield   usage example  here's how you might use these constants in another part of your application, for example, when processing a payment for a gold membership:  javascript // assuming this code is in src/routes/payment.js or src/services/payment.js const { membershipamount } = require('../utils/constants');  const goldmembershipcost = membershipamount.gold;  console.log(the cost for a gold membership is: $${goldmembershipcost});  // you would then use this cost in your payment processing logic // e.g., stripe.charges.create({ amount: goldmembershipcost, ... })

title: Razorpay Utility
content: razorpay utility  this utility file provides an initialized razorpay client instance, configured with environment variables for api keys. it centralizes the razorpay integration for the application.   overview  the razorpay.js file is responsible for setting up and exporting a preconfigured instance of the razorpay sdk. this allows other parts of the application, such as payment routes or services, to interact with the razorpay api without needing to manage the client initialization themselves.   parameters / configuration  this utility does not export a function that accepts parameters directly. instead, it relies on environment variables for configuration.  <warning the razorpay api keys are critical for processing payments. ensure that razorpay_key_id and razorpay_key_secret are securely stored in your environment variables and are never committed to version control. </warning  <paramfield name="razorpay_key_id" type="string" required   your razorpay api key id. </paramfield  <paramfield name="razorpay_key_secret" type="string" required   your razorpay api key secret. </paramfield   razorpay instance  this file exports a single, initialized instance of the razorpay client.   instance  an initialized razorpay client object.   usage example  javascript // in another file, e.g., src/routes/payment.js  const razorpayinstance = require("../utils/razorpay");  // example of creating a razorpay order async function createorder(amount, currency) {   try {     const order = await razorpayinstance.orders.create({       amount: amount  100, // amount in the smallest currency unit       currency: currency,       receipt: receipt_order_${date.now()},     });     return order;   } catch (error) {     console.error("error creating razorpay order:", error);     throw error;   } }  // ... rest of your payment logic

title: Email Sending Utility
content: email sending utility  this utility file provides functions for sending emails using the aws simple email service (ses). it abstracts the complexities of constructing ses commands and handles sending emails to specified recipients.   overview  the sendemail.js file is a utility that leverages the aws sdk for javascript to interact with amazon ses. its primary purpose is to facilitate sending emails from the backend application, abstracting the underlying ses api calls. this module is crucial for any feature requiring email notifications, such as account verification, password resets, or system alerts.   parameters / configuration  this utility does not directly accept configuration parameters upon import. instead, it relies on the preconfigured sesclient utility to establish a connection to aws ses.   functions   run()  sends an email using the configured aws ses client.  this function constructs an email message and sends it to the specified recipient using aws ses. it handles potential messagerejected errors specifically.  <info this function assumes that the sesclient has been properly configured with aws credentials and region. it also expects a valid toaddress and fromaddress to be used within its internal createsendemailcommand function. the html and text bodies, as well as the subject, are currently hardcoded within createsendemailcommand and would need customization for dynamic content. </info  javascript const { sesclient } = require("./sesclient"); // assumes sesclient is configured  const run = async () = {   // internal function to create the ses command   const createsendemailcommand = (toaddress, fromaddress) = {     return new sendemailcommand({       destination: {         toaddresses: [toaddress],       },       message: {         body: {           html: {             charset: "utf8",             data: "html_format_body", // todo: make dynamic           },           text: {             charset: "utf8",             data: "text_format_body", // todo: make dynamic           },         },         subject: {           charset: "utf8",           data: "email_subject", // todo: make dynamic         },       },       source: fromaddress,     });   };    const sendemailcommand = createsendemailcommand(     "eurydomeadvisorspvtltd@gmail.com", // placeholder recipient     "yashnirwan18@gmail.com",         // placeholder sender   );    try {     return await sesclient.send(sendemailcommand);   } catch (caught) {     if (caught instanceof error && caught.name === "messagerejected") {       / @type { import('@awssdk/clientses').messagerejected} /       const messagerejectederror = caught;       return messagerejectederror;     }     throw caught;   } };    usage example  here's an example of how you might call the run function from another part of your application to send an email.  <tip for dynamic email content, you would typically modify the createsendemailcommand function or pass content as parameters to the run function. </tip  javascript const { run } = require('../utils/sendemail'); // assuming this file is in src/utils  // ... within another module, e.g., a controller or service  const sendwelcomeemail = async (useremail) = {   try {     // in a real application, the fromaddress would likely come from configuration     const emailresult = await run(useremail, 'noreply@yourdomain.com');      if (emailresult.messageid) {       console.log(email sent successfully to ${useremail}. message id: ${emailresult.messageid});     } else {       console.error(failed to send email. rejected reason: ${emailresult.messagerejected});     }   } catch (error) {     console.error(error sending email:, error);   } };  // example usage: // sendwelcomeemail('newuser@example.com');    common errors / troubleshooting  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="messagerejected error"     this error typically occurs when aws ses rejects the email for reasons such as:     <ul       <lithe sender email address is not verified in ses.</li       <lithe recipient email address is not verified and ses is in sandbox mode.</li       <lithe email content violates ses sending policies.</li     </ul     <tip     ensure your sender (fromaddress) and recipient (toaddress) are verified in your aws ses console. if you are in the ses sandbox, you must verify all recipient email addresses.     </tip   </accordion   <accordion title="aws credentials error"     if you encounter errors related to authentication or authorization, it means the sesclient is not properly configured with valid aws credentials or permissions.     <warning     never hardcode aws credentials directly in your code. use environment variables or iam roles for secure credential management.     </warning   </accordion </accordiongroup

title: SES Client
content: ses client  this utility file configures and exports an aws ses (simple email service) client instance, making it readily available for use in sending emails throughout the application.   overview  the sesclient.js file initializes an aws ses client using environment variables for credentials and specifies the aws region. this centralizes the email sending configuration and ensures consistent usage across the backend. it's a crucial utility for any feature requiring email notifications or communication.   parameters / configuration  this file does not export a primary function that takes parameters directly. instead, it relies on environment variables for configuration.  <paramfield name="aws_access_key" type="string" required   your aws access key id. this is required for authenticating with aws services. </paramfield  <paramfield name="aws_ses_secret" type="string" required   your aws secret access key. this is required for authenticating with aws services. </paramfield  <paramfield name="region" type="string" default="useast1"   the aws region where your ses resources are configured. </paramfield  <warning   exposing your aws access key and secret access key directly in the code is a security risk. ensure these are stored securely in environment variables and never committed to your version control system. </warning   ses client export  this file exports a preconfigured aws ses client instance.   sesclient  the initialized aws ses client object.  javascript const { sesclient } = require("@awssdk/clientses");  const sesclient = new sesclient({   region: "useast1",   credentials: {     accesskeyid: process.env.aws_access_key,     secretaccesskey: process.env.aws_ses_secret,   }, });    usage example  this client is typically imported and used within other utility files or services that handle email sending.  javascript // in another file, e.g., src/utils/sendemail.js const { sesclient } = require("./sesclient"); const { sendemailcommand } = require("@awssdk/clientses");  async function sendwelcomeemail(recipientemail) {   const params = {     destination: {       toaddresses: [recipientemail],     },     message: {       body: {         html: {           charset: "utf8",           data: "<h1welcome to our service!</h1<pwe are excited to have you.</p",         },         text: {           charset: "utf8",           data: "welcome to our service! we are excited to have you.",         },       },       subject: {         charset: "utf8",         data: "welcome email",       },     },     source: process.env.aws_ses_sender_email, // ensure this is a verified ses email address   };    const command = new sendemailcommand(params);    try {     const data = await sesclient.send(command);     console.log("email sent successfully:", data);     return data;   } catch (error) {     console.error("error sending email:", error);     throw error;   } }  module.exports = { sendwelcomeemail };    common errors / troubleshooting  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="error: credentials must be provided"     this error indicates that your aws access key id and secret access key are not being properly loaded from environment variables. ensure that .env file is present in the root of your project and contains aws_access_key and aws_ses_secret with valid credentials. restart your application after updating the .env file.   </accordion   <accordion title="error: invalid parameter: source"     the source email address you are trying to send from has not been verified in your aws ses account. you need to verify the sender email address in the aws ses console before you can send emails from it.   </accordion   <accordion title="error: ses is not configured in the specified region"     the region environment variable might be set incorrectly or ses might not be enabled/configured in the region specified ("useast1" by default). doublecheck your aws region configuration and ensure ses is available and set up in that region for your account.   </accordion </accordiongroup

title: Socket Utilities
content: socket utilities  this file contains utility functions for initializing and managing realtime communication using socket.io. it handles user connections, chat room management, and message broadcasting.   overview  the socket.js utility is responsible for setting up and managing websocket connections for realtime features, primarily for chat functionality. it integrates with socket.io to handle connections, disconnections, joining chat rooms, and broadcasting messages between users. this utility is imported and used in src/app.js to establish the realtime communication layer for the application.   initialization  the initializesocket function sets up the socket.io server instance, configuring cors settings based on the environment and defining event listeners for various client interactions.  mdx <tip ensure your node_env environment variable is set correctly. for production, the origin is restricted to your live domain to prevent security vulnerabilities. </tip   <paramfield name="server" type="http.server"   the node.js http server instance to attach the socket.io server to. </paramfield  javascript const initializesocket = (server) = {   // ... socket.io setup code };    socket events  the following events are handled by the socket.io server:   connection  this event is triggered whenever a new client connects to the socket.io server. it logs the newly connected socket's id to the console.   joinchat  when a user wants to join a chat, this event is emitted. it generates a unique room name based on the sorted user ids of the participants and joins the socket to that room.  <paramfield name="userid" type="string" required   the id of the user initiating the join. </paramfield <paramfield name="targetuserid" type="string" required   the id of the user they wish to chat with. </paramfield  javascript socket.on("joinchat", ({ userid, targetuserid }) = {   const ids = [userid, targetuserid].sort();   const roomname = crypto     .createhash("sha256")     .update(ids.join(""))     .digest("hex");   socket.join(roomname);   console.log(user ${userid} joined room: ${roomname}); });   <note the room name is generated using sha256 hashing on the sorted participant ids. this ensures that regardless of which participant initiates the joinchat event, they will always join the same room for a given chat pair. </note   sendmessage  this event handles the broadcasting of chat messages. it first checks if a chat document exists between the sender and receiver. if not, it creates a new one. the message is then saved to the database, and finally, it's broadcast to all clients in the corresponding chat room, excluding the sender.  <paramfield name="senderid" type="string" required   the id of the user sending the message. </paramfield <paramfield name="targetuserid" type="string" required   the id of the user receiving the message. </paramfield <paramfield name="text" type="string" required   the content of the message. </paramfield  javascript socket.on("sendmessage", async ({ senderid, targetuserid, text }) = {   try {     if (!senderid || !targetuserid || !text) {       return console.error("sendmessage event received with missing data.");     }      let chat = await chat.findone({       participants: { $all: [senderid, targetuserid] },     });      if (!chat) {       chat = new chat({         participants: [senderid, targetuserid],         messages: [],       });     }      chat.messages.push({ senderid: senderid, text: text });     await chat.save();      const ids = [senderid, targetuserid].sort();     const roomname = crypto       .createhash("sha256")       .update(ids.join(""))       .digest("hex");      socket.broadcast       .to(roomname)       .emit("messagereceived", { senderid, text });   } catch (err) {     console.error("error in sendmessage:", err);   } });   <warning ensure senderid, targetuserid, and text are always provided. missing data can lead to errors in chat history creation and message delivery. </warning   disconnect  this event is triggered when a client disconnects from the socket.io server. it logs the disconnected socket's id.   usage example  this utility is typically imported and used in your main application file (src/app.js) to set up the realtime communication layer.  javascript // in src/app.js const http = require('http'); const initializesocket = require('./utils/socket');  const server = http.createserver(app); // assuming 'app' is your express app const io = initializesocket(server);  // ... rest of your server setup    dependencies  this utility depends on the following modules:     socket.io: for realtime bidirectional eventbased communication.    ../models/chat: the mongoose model for storing chat data.    crypto: node.js builtin module for generating secure room names.   environment variables  the cors origin is determined by the node_env environment variable:     production: uses https://www.yourliveappdomain.com.    any other value (e.g., development): uses http://localhost:5173.  <info it is crucial to set the node_env environment variable correctly for your deployment. </info

title: Input Validation Utilities
content: input validation utilities  this file contains utility functions for validating user input data across various api endpoints, ensuring data integrity and security before it's processed by the application.   overview  the validation.js module provides helper functions to validate data received in api requests. it leverages the validator library to check for common data formats like email addresses and strong passwords, and enforces custom business logic rules. this module is crucial for maintaining data quality and preventing invalid or malicious input from reaching the core application logic or database.   parameters / configuration  this file exports functions that do not accept direct configuration parameters but instead operate on the req object from an express.js request.   functions   validatesignupdata  validates the data provided for user signup.  <warning this function throws errors upon encountering invalid data. ensure that the calling route handler is prepared to catch and handle these errors gracefully, returning appropriate http status codes and messages to the client. </warning   parameters  <paramfield name="req" type="object" required the express.js request object. the validation logic will inspect req.body. <expandable title="req.body properties" <paramfield name="req.body.firstname" type="string" required the user's first name. must be at least 4 characters long. </paramfield <paramfield name="req.body.lastname" type="string" required the user's last name. </paramfield <paramfield name="req.body.emailid" type="string" required the user's email address. must be a valid email format. </paramfield <paramfield name="req.body.password" type="string" required the user's password. must be at least 6 characters long. </paramfield <paramfield name="req.body.age" type="number" the user's age. </paramfield <paramfield name="req.body.gender" type="string" the user's gender. accepts "male", "female", or "other" (caseinsensitive). </paramfield </expandable </paramfield   example  javascript // in a route handler (e.g., src/routes/auth.js) const { validatesignupdata } = require('../utils/validation');  app.post('/signup', (req, res) = {   try {     validatesignupdata(req);     // proceed with user creation if validation passes     res.status(201).json({ message: 'user data validated successfully.' });   } catch (error) {     res.status(400).json({ error: error.message });   } });    validateeditprofiledata  checks if the fields provided for editing a user's profile are allowed.   parameters  <paramfield name="req" type="object" required the express.js request object. the validation logic will inspect req.body. <expandable title="req.body properties" this function checks for the presence of any of the following fields in req.body:  firstname  lastname  emailid  about  skills  age  photourl  gender </expandable </paramfield   returns  <responsefield name="iseditallowed" type="boolean" returns true if all fields in req.body are present in the allowededitfields array, false otherwise. </responsefield   example  javascript // in a route handler (e.g., src/routes/profile.js) const { validateeditprofiledata } = require('../utils/validation');  app.put('/profile', (req, res) = {   const isallowed = validateeditprofiledata(req);   if (!isallowed) {     return res.status(400).json({ error: 'some fields are not allowed for editing.' });   }   // proceed with profile update if validation passes   res.json({ message: 'profile edit data is valid.' }); });    common errors / troubleshooting  <accordiongroup   <accordion title="what happens if validatesignupdata throws an error?"     if validatesignupdata encounters an invalid field or format, it will throw an error object with a descriptive message. the route handler that calls validatesignupdata should use a try...catch block to catch this error and return an appropriate http 400 (bad request) response to the client, including the error message.   </accordion   <accordion title="what are the allowed fields for editing a profile with validateeditprofiledata?"     the validateeditprofiledata function specifically allows the following fields for editing: firstname, lastname, emailid, about, skills, age, photourl, and gender. if any other field is present in the request body, the function will return false.   </accordion   <accordion title="why is email validation important?"     email validation is critical for user account management, communication, and security. it ensures that users can be contacted, that password reset mechanisms work correctly, and prevents the system from storing malformed email addresses that could lead to issues with mail delivery or processing.   </accordion </accordiongroup
